summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for worsening bilateral lower extremity pain, erythema, and malodorous discharge concerning for infection. Wound culture confirmed moderate growth of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and he was treated with a seven-day course of IV piperacillin-tazobactam. He developed mild antibiotic-associated diarrhea, managed with loperamide, and transient elevations in creatinine and liver enzymes, which resolved by discharge. Wound care and dermatology optimized his dressing regimen, including acetic acid soaks and alternating topical metronidazole and gentamicin. His pain improved, infection markers normalized, and he was discharged home on oral azithromycin with continued home medications, including IL-2 as part of a clinical trial, and close outpatient follow-up.
